q2_gaps: definite-singular generic subject ("The cold-threshold wind is a cutting north wind"): the instruction set states no rule for when a definite singular NP denotes a KIND (Inheritance on a bare kind symbol) rather than a specific referent (witness + Member) — the definite-description rule says "picks out a specific thing" without saying how to tell, and only the "the dodo is extinct" KindProperty example touches the definite-generic case
notes: Fusing "cutting" into cutting_north_wind is a judgment call against the "incidental description" bar (a dented pail), but the exposed modifier genus (Inheritance cutting_north_wind cutting) preserves the same inheritances either way. Compound handling is otherwise right: genus wind on both compounds, noun-modifier cold_threshold left unexposed, positional north and participial-adjective cutting exposed.
